Cyberpunk 2077 is one of those games where I can see why people are into it, but it just never really clicked for me. I'd describe my experience as a bit of a love/hate relationship. The futuristic cyberpunk setting is interesting, and Night City definitely has its own identity, but after a while the novelty wears off. The combat is decent enough, but it gets repetitive pretty quickly. It never felt bad, just not interesting enough to keep me engaged for long stretches. The music was another big miss for me. It leans heavily into a punk-techno style that just isn't my thing. The combat music in particular got irritating after a while and often made fights feel more annoying than exciting. Driving is fine. I didn't hate it, but I've played plenty of games that do it much better. It gets the job done, but it's not something I'd point to as a strength. Overall, I respect what the game is trying to do, and I can appreciate the world they've built, but I just didn't find it all that enjoyable. It's not a terrible game, but it's one I'll probably forget about long before I revisit it.

I bought this game at launch, AFTER seeing the spew of (well deserved) negativity online regarding bugs, performance issues, etc. I bought it as an investment; I did this because I am a big fan of CD Project Red and I know what a hardworking and talented team they have there, having previous played TW3. I messed around for a few hours, came to understand the nature of the task the developers were going to face if they were going to repair their game and set it down.

A long time later and here we are: I picked up the game again some time ago after Phantom Liberty dropped. ~340 hours and 3 campaigns later here I am to recommend this game to anyone who will listen. Please, if you are thinking about it or are held back by past impressions of a defunct broken product PLAY THIS GAME. 

This is currently my favorite game of all time, and it is well earned. The world of Night City is the most dense and alive universe I have ever been allowed to immerse myself in. The writing, characters, themes, and story pull heart strings in a way few other games ever could manage to. And most importantly: It is fun. The gameplay is so damn addicting and meshes with the overall vibe of the world and your place in it so well, seriously. Whether i am playing a netrunner frying enemies (or bystanders) seamlessly in milliseconds on my way to an objective or an edgerunning solo blasting and chopping my way in slo mo through a crowd of flesh and chrome during a merc gig I am having a fucking blast.

This is all without mentioning that CDPR created one of the best DLCs of all time in Phantom Liberty. A spy thriller set in the bad part of town's bad part of town where you can choose between multiple endings, all of which leave that metallic, cheap, bittersweet flavor of "wtf did I just do" in your mouth that the world of Cyberpunk is always so ready to serve you yet never running out of. 

In conclusion: Buy this game. If you manage to enjoy it casually and play it every once in a while
